pages.text: They had finished shaking olives from the trees. Olives covered the big net underneath.
Now they needed to lift it and gather the olives in the middle. Lulu held a corner. "This corner is mine!"
Across the net, Uncle Nino called, "I can do it alone! I will take two corners."
Uncle Beppo brought a stick. "We used to roll it up." Aunt Rosa kept taking and dropping corners. "Here? There?"
Uncle Nino pulled two corners. The net tilted, and olives rushed to one side.
While the three cried "This way!" and "That way!", the net tilted more.
Lulu called the cousins. "One corner each! Lift together on one, two!"
"One, two!" Four corners rose at once. The olives rolled into the middle.
An olive mountain filled the net's center. The three grown-ups held the edges too—at last, just as they were told.
